claims.text: Nanoscale chemical ordering governs the balance between transition sharpness and hysteresis in as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys.
Controlled post-deposition annealing below the order-disorder threshold will modestly increase nanoscale chemical ordering.
Increasing nanoscale order will disperse the magnetostructural transformation over a wider temperature range.
Dispersing the transformation will reduce hysteretic losses while maintaining a useful magnetocaloric effect.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal state.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition.
Sub-threshold post-deposition annealing can modify ordered-domain sizes without inducing secondary phases.
The relevant structural mediators are the degree of nanoscale chemical order and the distribution and size of ordered domains and interfaces.
Annealing-induced chemical order reduces the nucleation barrier for the magnetostructural transition.
The reduced nucleation barrier spreads the entropy change over a broader temperature range.
A dispersed transition lowers hysteretic energy loss by making magnetoelastic coupling less abrupt.
Annealed samples should show a broader magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples should have lower hysteresis loop area or coercive field than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing should slightly reduce the peak magnetic entropy change while preserving the overall magnetocaloric response.
The annealed material should provide improved heat-exchange rates in low-field cooling cycles.
The proposed trends apply only near the transition temperature, at low magnetic fields, and within a similar non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi composition range.
Large composition changes, high applied fields, or annealing that produces secondary phases may invalidate the predicted trends.
